claims.text: What the image looks like Free air under diaphragm; Rigler / double-wall sign; football sign in infants → pneumoperitoneum (perforation)
claims.quote: Free air under diaphragm; Rigler / double-wall sign; football sign in infants Pneumoperitoneum (perforation)

claims.text: On chest X-ray: free air under the right hemidiaphragm → pneumoperitoneum (perforation)
claims.quote: Free air under right hemidiaphragm Pneumoperitoneum (perforation)

claims.text: Buzzword: Rigler / double-wall sign on AXR → pneumoperitoneum
Buzzword: football sign on AXR (infant supine) → massive pneumoperitoneum
claims.quote: Football sign AXR (infant supine) Massive pneumoperitoneum

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) Confirm the view: is an upright present? Free air is best seen on an upright CXR or left lateral decubitus
claims.quote: Confirm view - upright present? (Free air best on upright CXR or L lateral decubitus)

claims.text: Free air: under the diaphragm; Rigler sign (gas on both sides of the bowel wall); football sign in infants
claims.quote: Free air: under diaphragm; Rigler sign (gas on both sides of bowel wall); football sign in infants.

claims.text: An abdominal series (supine and upright abdominal plus chest films) may be diagnostic, showing free air under the diaphragm in 50 to 75%, more often as time passes; a lateral chest film is more sensitive for free air than a PA film
claims.quote: An abdominal series (supine and upright abdominal radiographs and chest radiographs) may be diagnostic, showing free air under the diaphragm in 50 to 75% of cases (1, 2). As time passes, this sign becomes more common. A lateral chest radiograph is more sensitive for free air than a posteroanterior radiograph.

claims.text: If nondiagnostic: abdominal CT, usually with oral and IV and/or rectal contrast, may help; no barium if perforation is suspected
claims.quote: If the abdominal series is nondiagnostic, abdominal CT usually with oral and IV and/or rectal contrast may be helpful. Barium should not be used if perforation is suspected.

claims.text: Peptic ulcer perforation can occur without prior ulcer symptoms, and sometimes no free air is visible on the film
claims.quote: Peptic ulcer disease | Can occur in patients with no previous history of ulcer symptoms Sometimes no free air is visible on radiograph
claims.locator: Some Causes of Gastrointestinal Tract Perforation table, Stomach or duodenum

claims.text: Causes Any part of the GI tract may perforate, releasing gastric or intestinal contents into the peritoneal space
claims.quote: Any part of the gastrointestinal tract may become perforated, releasing gastric or intestinal contents into the peritoneal space.

claims.text: Intestine: strangulating obstruction; possibly acute appendicitis and Meckel diverticulitis (with these, free air is rarely visible on radiographs)
claims.quote: Intestine | Strangulating obstruction | ― | Possibly acute appendicitis and Meckel diverticulitis | Free air rarely visible on radiographs
claims.locator: Some Causes of Gastrointestinal Tract Perforation table

claims.text: Colon: obstruction (typically perforates at the cecum; high risk with colon ≥ 13 cm or on prednisone/immunosuppressants), diverticulitis, inflammatory bowel disease, toxic megacolon, sometimes spontaneous
claims.quote: Colon | Obstruction | Typically perforates at cecum High risk: Colon ≥ 13 cm diameter, patients receiving prednisone or other immunosuppressants (symptoms and signs may be minimal in this group) | Diverticulitis | ― | Inflammatory bowel disease (ulcerative colitis, Crohn disease) | ― | Toxic megacolon | ― | Sometimes spontaneous
claims.locator: Some Causes of Gastrointestinal Tract Perforation table

claims.text: Symptoms Esophageal, gastric or duodenal perforation tends to be sudden and catastrophic: acute abdomen with severe generalized pain, tenderness and peritoneal signs; pain may radiate to the shoulder
claims.quote: Esophageal, gastric, or duodenal perforation tends to manifest suddenly and catastrophically, with abrupt onset of acute abdomen with severe generalized abdominal pain, tenderness, and peritoneal signs. Pain may radiate to the shoulder.

claims.text: Other sites often perforate during another painful inflammatory condition; small and walled off by the omentum, so pain often develops gradually and may be localized
claims.quote: Perforation at other gastrointestinal sites often occurs in the setting of other painful, inflammatory conditions. Because such perforations are often small initially and frequently walled off by the omentum, pain often develops gradually and may be localized.

claims.text: All types: nausea, vomiting and anorexia are common; bowel sounds are quiet to absent
claims.quote: In all types of perforation, nausea, vomiting, and anorexia are common. Bowel sounds are quiet to absent.

claims.text: Treatment and next step Her chart: emergent surgical exploration
Immediate surgery: peritonitis mortality rises rapidly the longer treatment is delayed; if an abscess or inflammatory mass has formed, the procedure may be limited to drainage
claims.quote: If a perforation is noted, immediate surgery is necessary because mortality caused by peritonitis increases rapidly the longer treatment is delayed. If an abscess or an inflammatory mass has formed, the procedure may be limited to drainage of the abscess.

claims.text: A nasogastric tube is sometimes placed before surgery; IV fluid and electrolyte replacement; broad-spectrum IV antibiotics effective against intestinal flora
claims.quote: A nasogastric tube is sometimes inserted before operation. Patients with signs of volume depletion should have urine output monitored with a catheter. Fluid status is maintained by adequate IV fluid and electrolyte replacement. Broad-spectrum IV antibiotics effective against intestinal flora should be given.

notes.issue: 'free air rarely visible' could read as covering strangulating obstruction; in the table it belongs only to appendicitis/Meckel
